data.G: Reference starting point: supplied baseline commit 9eed4bd28ac4ef71f9120cc0c1658bbc071e7e96; no source changes made in planning. After research closes, compare correctly validated candidates using the official latency criterion, integrate the selected measured implementation, then request independent confirmation of final G.
data.analysis: Choose N=3 because the baseline suggests three distinct single-kernel strategies worth testing, not to meet a preset tree count. The measured baseline is correct, with three samples averaging 3.494 μs; no profiling or child measurements are available, so coalescing and synchronization are hypotheses to test rather than proven bottlenecks. In the supplied kernel, a block spans 4 x positions and 64 y positions, uses shared memory, and executes two block barriers. The proposed trees separately test eliminating shared memory, improving x-wide shared tiling, and reusing loads across multiple y outputs in registers. The CUDA 12.6.3 Best Practices Guide discusses coalescing and strided access (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-best-practices-guide/index.html, §9.2.1); this supports the rationale, not a performance prediction. Preserve the supplied 64³ FP32 operation, coefficients, exact y-halo convention (including the period-63 endpoint handling), tolerance, full C output, entry point, and buffer/allocation constraints. The supplied target is NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3; no exact compiler version or device-counter evidence is available.

children.objective: Implement and measure a single-pass direct-global stencil with one output per thread and no shared memory or block-wide barriers. Map warp lanes to contiguous x elements; compare practical launch mappings and unroll the eight neighbor terms. Reproduce the baseline y-halo mapping for every offset, produce all 64³ outputs from current A on every call, and use no extra launch or allocation. Validate against the independent oracle and compare full-run event latency with the baseline.
children.subject: Coalesced direct-global stencil without shared memory

children.objective: Implement and measure an x-wide shared-memory y tile, using warp lanes over contiguous x positions and a small y output tile with the required radius-4 halo. Explore tile dimensions and reuse while minimizing barriers and redundant halo loads. Keep the stencil, exact endpoint/halo behavior, output coverage, and API correct; use no new allocations or launches beyond the single stencil launch. Record correctness and full-run latency.
children.subject: X-coalesced shared-memory tiling with y halo

children.objective: Implement and measure register-blocked y outputs: assign contiguous x elements across warp lanes and have each thread compute multiple nearby y outputs, reusing their overlapping input neighborhood in registers rather than shared memory. Explore a small number of outputs per thread and suitable launch geometry; preserve exact coefficients and baseline halo mapping, compute every output from current A, and use no additional allocation or launch. Compare oracle correctness and full-run latency.
children.subject: Register reuse across multiple y outputs
